meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes before a client call. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
A timed class piece and an essay written over a weekend are different things, Hale. Do you have the September 24 sample with you, and was Owen asked about any of this before the zero went in?
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay. I'm writing that down, Hale: the checker is off the table. Now show me the version history, with the dates and times on it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed in the meeting to take the checker off the table and rely on Owen's writing and the version history. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology for the way Owen found out, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Still at her opening position, with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see the version history, and a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under 4.4 would have been the fair outcome, which you never reached.
What moved her: You dropped the checker yourself without being pushed, which gave her a flat okay and a note written down, because it removed her strongest argument and showed you would work from the documents.
What cost ground: You never answered who decided on the zero or whether Owen was spoken to first, and you never owned entering it before calling home, so she kept returning to procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed far from that night because you gave no times from the version history, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after her first question, own in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put the version history in front of her with its dates and times.
